justification: Assessment returned INVALID and, among its listed defects, explicitly names the ground-truth flaw: it states the reverse ('only if') direction is wrong and gives exactly the ground-truth witness -- the single 2-cycle v1->v2->v1, which is cyclic yet has the unique transitive reduction {(v1,v2),(v2,v1)}, contradicting the claim that cyclic graphs admit multiple reductions. It also notes line 0053's R2 is undefined for k=2 (no v3), which is the same breakdown. Its designated earliest failing step (base case 0023-0025) is an additional, independently correct observation (a direct edge u->v can be shadowed by u->w->v, so length-1 shortest path does not imply (u,v) in R), so it does not undermine the match; the target defect is covered with a valid witness.
